A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VoMP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–H support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original mechanical-property prediction, mass estimation, runtime, MatVAE reconstruction, ablation, and simulation results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds public-subset evaluation results and a robot-interaction simulation.

M1.justification: MatVAE, voxel feature aggregation, the Geometry Transformer, training objectives, inference, and Gaussian-splat voxelization remain unchanged. The added simulation uses the existing pipeline.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 and new Figure 14 add a robot interacting with multiple objects in a Gaussian-splat scene, extending the demonstrated interaction scenarios. MTD, GVM, and ABO-500 coverage is otherwise retained; the public-subset evaluation uses existing GVM data.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain NeRF2Physics, PUGS, Phys4DGen*, and the limited Pixie comparisons. New public-subset Tables 2–3 use the same comparator set as the corresponding full-dataset mechanical-property evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on GVM with vegetation excluded, reporting both object-averaged and voxel-averaged errors in Tables 2–3. These aggregation schemes already existed for the full test set. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 14 adds a qualitative case study of robot interaction in a multi-object Gaussian-splat scene, including predicted properties and voxelized objects. Existing component ablations, latent-space analyses, and material-error simulation studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report uncertainty values, runtime measurements across 100 runs, and confidence bands in the simulation analyses. The new subset tables follow the existing reporting format without introducing new run-count, seed, or statistical-testing information.

E6.justification: Original results remain unchanged, including Figure 6 and v1 Table 2, now v2 Table 4. New public-subset Tables 2–3 report density ADE values of 142.7017 and 113.4683, respectively; retained full-set values are 142.6949 and 113.3807. These are additional results under different data selection, not same-setting performance changes. Figure 14 adds qualitative simulation results.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, metric definitions, normalizing-flow and KL derivations, algorithms, and simulation equations are retained. No substantive mathematical assumption, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: feed-forward volumetric property prediction across representations, a material latent space, an annotation pipeline and benchmark, and improved accuracy and speed over prior methods.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the public-subset results as closely matching full-dataset results and explicitly describes its voxelizer as effective on complex, noisy splats. Appendix E.1 strengthens the annotation interpretation from performing very well to approaching human-annotator performance, although the supporting table is unchanged. Existing resolution and isotropy limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 discusses releasing the benchmark; v2 newly documents that the publicly released dataset excludes vegetation because that subset cannot be shared. This clarifies reproduction scope. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and training times remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning in Section 2 and Appendix H are unchanged, including comparisons of the work's scope with Pixie, SOPHY, and PhysX-3D.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited spelling and terminology corrections, adds acknowledgments and short explanatory passages, and replaces the running title with an ICLR 2026 publication header. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two public-subset result tables and the robot-scene Figure 14. Existing displays are retained with some repositioning, spacing changes, and subsequent renumbering; there is no extensive redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency by documenting the vegetation release restriction and reporting public-subset estimates, while the robot-scene example adds application evidence. The gains are limited: new voxel-averaged Table 3 repeats object-averaged baseline entries without explaining their recomputation, and the stronger human-annotator interpretation has no additional validation. The original method and supporting results remain intact.
